articles.title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
articles.summary: The asteroid's surface was transformed after a spacecraft was deliberately crashed into it four years ago
articles.content:
The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface.

The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022. The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course.

Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision.

"The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team.

"It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened. And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful."

The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h).

It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 6,200 miles long (10,000km), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space.

Dimorphos is about 150m (500ft) wide and was partly chosen as the target because it is one of an asteroid pair - it orbits around a larger space rock called Didymos, which is about 730m (2,400ft) wide.

The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid.

Before the collision, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes.
articles.reasoning: The article reports a successful planetary defense test where a spacecraft deliberately impacted an asteroid, creating a large crater and altering its orbit. This demonstrates a significant technological and scientific achievement with broad implications for Earth's safety against asteroid threats. The story is focused, detailed, and highlights a major breakthrough in space exploration and planetary defense.
articles.personality_title: Spacecraft crash creates giant crater on asteroid, proving planetary defense works
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In 2022, NASA tested a new way to protect Earth from dangerous asteroids by crashing a spacecraft into a small space rock called Dimorphos. This asteroid was not a threat, but the test aimed to see if its path could be changed.

**What happened** – Four years later, the European Space Agency’s spacecraft Hera took close-up pictures of Dimorphos. These images showed a huge crater on the asteroid’s surface, almost as big as the asteroid itself. The original crash by NASA’s Dart spacecraft hit Dimorphos at 14,000 mph, pushing the asteroid and creating a trail of debris visible from Earth.

**Impact** – This event proved that we can change an asteroid’s orbit by hitting it with a spacecraft. Before the crash, Dimorphos took nearly 12 hours to orbit its larger companion asteroid, Didymos. After the impact, its orbit became about 33 minutes shorter. This is the first time humans have successfully altered the path of a space rock, which is a major step in protecting Earth from future asteroid threats.

**What's next step** – Scientists will use Hera’s data to learn more about how the crash changed Dimorphos. This will help improve technology and strategies for defending Earth if a dangerous asteroid is ever found. The mission also shows how countries can work together on space safety.

**One-sentence takeaway** – NASA and ESA’s spacecraft missions proved it’s possible to safely change an asteroid’s course, opening new ways to protect Earth from space hazards.
articles.personality_title_fr: Un crash de vaisseau spatial crée un énorme cratère sur un astéroïde, prouvant l'efficacité de la défense planétaire
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – En 2022, la NASA a testé une nouvelle méthode pour protéger la Terre des astéroïdes dangereux en percutant une petite roche spatiale appelée Dimorphos. Cet astéroïde ne représentait pas de menace, mais le test visait à voir si sa trajectoire pouvait être modifiée.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Quatre ans plus tard, le vaisseau spatial Hera de l’Agence spatiale européenne a pris des photos rapprochées de Dimorphos. Ces images ont montré un énorme cratère à la surface de l’astéroïde, presque aussi grand que l’astéroïde lui-même. Le crash original du vaisseau Dart de la NASA a frappé Dimorphos à 22 000 km/h, poussant l’astéroïde et créant une traînée de débris visible depuis la Terre.

**Impact** – Cet événement a prouvé que l’on peut modifier l’orbite d’un astéroïde en le percutant avec un vaisseau spatial. Avant le crash, Dimorphos mettait près de 12 heures pour orbiter autour de son astéroïde compagnon plus grand, Didymos. Après l’impact, son orbite a été raccourcie d’environ 33 minutes. C’est la première fois que l’homme modifie avec succès la trajectoire d’un corps spatial, une avancée majeure pour protéger la Terre.

**Prochaine étape** – Les scientifiques utiliseront les données de Hera pour mieux comprendre comment le crash a changé Dimorphos. Cela permettra d’améliorer les technologies et les stratégies pour défendre la Terre si un astéroïde dangereux est détecté. Cette mission montre aussi la coopération internationale en matière de sécurité spatiale.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Les missions spatiales de la NASA et de l’ESA ont prouvé qu’il est possible de changer en toute sécurité la trajectoire d’un astéroïde, ouvrant de nouvelles voies pour protéger la Terre des dangers de l’espace.
articles.personality_title_es: Una nave espacial crea un cráter gigante en un asteroide, demostrando que la defensa planetaria funciona
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En 2022, la NASA probó una nueva forma de proteger la Tierra de asteroides peligrosos estrellando una nave espacial contra una pequeña roca llamada Dimorphos. Este asteroide no representaba una amenaza, pero la prueba buscaba ver si se podía cambiar su camino.

**Qué pasó** – Cuatro años después, la nave Hera de la Agencia Espacial Europea tomó fotos cercanas de Dimorphos. Estas imágenes mostraron un cráter enorme en la superficie del asteroide, casi tan grande como el propio asteroide. El choque original de la nave Dart de la NASA impactó Dimorphos a 22,000 km/h, empujando el asteroide y creando una estela de escombros visible desde la Tierra.

**Impacto** – Este evento demostró que se puede cambiar la órbita de un asteroide al chocar con él una nave espacial. Antes del choque, Dimorphos tardaba casi 12 horas en orbitar alrededor de su asteroide mayor, Didymos. Después del impacto, su órbita se acortó en unos 33 minutos. Es la primera vez que los humanos cambian con éxito el camino de una roca espacial, un paso importante para proteger la Tierra.

**Próximo paso** – Los científicos usarán los datos de Hera para aprender más sobre cómo el choque cambió a Dimorphos. Esto ayudará a mejorar la tecnología y las estrategias para defender la Tierra si alguna vez se encuentra un asteroide peligroso. La misión también muestra cómo los países pueden trabajar juntos para la seguridad espacial.

**Conclusión en una frase** – Las misiones de NASA y ESA demostraron que es posible cambiar de forma segura la trayectoria de un asteroide, abriendo nuevas formas de proteger la Tierra de peligros del espacio.

articles.title: China's Shenzhou-24 carries Pakistan's first astronaut into space
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former fighter pilot, is the first foreigner to join a Chinese crewed space mission.
articles.content:
China launched its Shenzhou-24 space mission on Wednesday carrying three astronauts to its Tiangong space station, including Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreigner to join a Chinese crewed space mission.

Beijing said it hopes the flight will strengthen ties with Islamabad, as the two countries mark 75 years of co-operation in space.

Speaking to reporters at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, Ali said he was "carrying the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis".

The mission, which also comprises of commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi, took off at 08:18 (00:18 GMT) from the Gobi desert. Minutes later, it was declared a "complete success".

While in space, the Shenzhou-24 crew will carry out experiments and test technology in fields like aerospace medicine, combustion and study the effects of space on living organisms.
articles.reasoning: The article reports a significant milestone in international space cooperation with Pakistan's first astronaut joining a Chinese crewed mission, symbolizing strengthened ties and advancing space exploration with scientific experiments aboard Tiangong station.
articles.personality_title: Pakistan’s first astronaut joins China’s Shenzhou-24 mission to space
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – China has been sending astronauts to its Tiangong space station as part of its growing space program. This mission is special because it includes the first astronaut from Pakistan, showing a new step in international cooperation in space.

**What happened** – On Wednesday, China launched the Shenzhou-24 mission from the Gobi desert. The crew includes three astronauts: Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Muhammad Zeeshan Ali from Pakistan. Ali, a former fighter pilot, is the first foreign astronaut to join a Chinese crewed space mission. The launch was successful and took place early in the morning.

**Impact** – This mission marks a milestone for Pakistan as it sends its first astronaut into space, symbolizing closer ties between China and Pakistan. It also allows scientists to conduct important experiments on the Tiangong space station. These experiments will explore how space affects living things, medicine, and how fire behaves without gravity.

**What’s next step** – During their time in space, the astronauts will carry out scientific tests and technology checks. The success of this mission could lead to more international partnerships and further scientific discoveries from the Tiangong station.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Pakistan’s first astronaut has joined China’s Shenzhou-24 mission, marking a new chapter in space cooperation and scientific research aboard the Tiangong space station.

Ali, ancien pilote de chasse, est le premier astronaute étranger à participer à une mission spatiale habitée chinoise. Le lancement a réussi et a eu lieu tôt le matin.

Elle permet aussi de réaliser des expériences scientifiques importantes à bord de la station Tiangong. **En une phrase** – Le premier astronaute pakistanais a rejoint la mission Shenzhou-24 de la Chine, marquant un nouveau chapitre de coopération spatiale et de recherche scientifique à bord de la station Tiangong.
articles.personality_title_es: El primer astronauta de Pakistán se une a la misión china Shenzhou-24 en el espacio

articles.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
articles.summary: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving.    Recent testing points to strawberries, […]
articles.content:
As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving.

Strawberries (left) grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers (center) and lemon basil (right) grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. NASA

Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water. These capabilities will become increasingly important as crewed missions extend farther from our home planet.

While space crop research advances on Earth, capabilities are also expanding in space. A new investigation from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division is set to launch to the International Space Station, where the first-of-its-kind prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing crop production systems that could grow crops like these for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions.

Sweet space strawberries

Strawberries are among the few sweet fruits under consideration for spaceflight and are nutritious, aromatic, and self-pollinating.

Researchers at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida are growing strawberries in flight-like growth chambers to evaluate the potential space crop, and NASA partners at The Australian Research Council Centre for Excellence in Plants for Space also are helping expand knowledge of space strawberries.

Researchers at NASA Kennedy, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Western Australia recently tested a wild strawberry against NASA’s leading strawberry candidate, ‘Delizz,’ to see which thrived better under simulated space conditions.

Delizz and the wild strawberry produced very different fruits, according to a study published in September in the journal Life Sciences in Space Research. Delizz grew large, red fruit, while the wild strawberry produced small, yellow fruit due to a recessive genetic mutation.

But looks are not everything. When grown from a seed, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds, flowers, and fruit as Delizz. Ultimately, however, NASA’s pick kept its top spot, as the wild strawberry grew too many runners that would take up valuable room aboard a spacecraft.

Cucumbers show promise

Many crops have been grown in space, but none so far have come from the gourd family. Cucumbers could be the first.

Before crops like cucumbers can be grown and eaten in space, they must undergo extensive testing. NASA-funded researchers recently evaluated cucumbers for their growth, yield, and nutrition under spaceflight conditions.

The researchers found that while the plants showed some signs of enlarged leaves, they produced a steady stream of edible fruit, according to a study published in August in the journal HortScience.

Offering a variety of crops, such as cucumbers, not only benefits astronauts’ diets and mental well-being, but it also increases plant biodiversity, which can improve the likelihood of crop success on long-duration missions.

Spicing up spaceflight

Herbs can spice up life in space, turning a bland meal into a bold one.

Lemon basil, an edible herb with a citrus scent and taste, is making strides in testing at NASA Kennedy.

Researchers report that lemon basil passed its preliminary round of space crop testing and successfully underwent seed sanitization, which is required before spaceflight to remove microorganisms from the seeds. Lemon basil’s next steps include assessing its growth in plant pillows, which can house plants aboard the space station.

Menu fatigue can quickly become a problem for astronauts, but fresh herbs like lemon basil help transform packaged meals into something new and satisfying, supporting human health and performance in space.
articles.reasoning: The article reports on NASA's research into growing nutritious crops like strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil for future long-duration space missions. This has broad significance for human health and sustainability in space exploration, providing fresh food, oxygen production, and psychological benefits for astronauts. The story is focused, detailed, and highlights a tangible advancement with meaningful impact on future crewed missions to the Moon and Mars.
articles.personality_title: NASA studies strawberries, cucumbers, and herbs for fresh food on Moon and Mars missions
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – NASA is preparing for long trips to the Moon and Mars. To help astronauts stay healthy and happy far from Earth, scientists are looking for crops that can grow in space and provide fresh food.

**What happened** – Researchers have been testing strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil in special growth chambers that copy space conditions. They found that strawberries like the 'Delizz' variety grow well and produce tasty fruit. Cucumbers, a new type of space crop, also grew steady fruit. Lemon basil, an herb with a lemon smell, passed early tests and will be tested further on the International Space Station.

**Impact** – Growing these crops in space is important because they not only provide fresh food but also help recycle air and water inside spacecraft. Fresh herbs and fruits can make meals more enjoyable, which helps astronauts avoid boredom with their food. This variety also supports their health and mental well-being during long missions.

**What's next step** – NASA will continue testing these plants on the International Space Station using a new growth chamber. This will give more information on how to successfully grow food on the Moon or Mars. Scientists will also study how to manage space for plants so they don’t take up too much room.

**One-sentence takeaway** – NASA’s tests with strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil bring fresh, healthy food closer to astronauts on future Moon and Mars missions.
articles.personality_title_fr: La NASA étudie fraises, concombres et herbes pour des repas frais lors des missions sur la Lune et Mars
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – La NASA prépare de longs voyages vers la Lune et Mars. Pour aider les astronautes à rester en bonne santé et de bonne humeur loin de la Terre, des scientifiques recherchent des cultures pouvant pousser dans l’espace et offrir des aliments frais.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Des chercheurs ont testé des fraises, des concombres et du basilic citron dans des chambres de culture qui reproduisent les conditions spatiales. Ils ont découvert que les fraises comme la variété « Delizz » poussent bien et donnent des fruits savoureux. Les concombres, une nouvelle culture spatiale, ont aussi produit des fruits réguliers. Le basilic citron, une herbe au parfum citronné, a passé les premiers tests et sera testé davantage sur la Station spatiale internationale.

**Impact** – Cultiver ces plantes dans l’espace est important car elles fournissent non seulement de la nourriture fraîche, mais aident aussi à recycler l’air et l’eau à bord des vaisseaux. Les herbes et fruits frais rendent les repas plus agréables, ce qui aide les astronautes à ne pas se lasser de leur nourriture. Cette variété soutient aussi leur santé et leur bien-être mental pendant les longues missions.

**Prochaine étape** – La NASA poursuivra les tests de ces plantes sur la Station spatiale internationale avec une nouvelle chambre de culture. Cela donnera plus d’informations pour réussir à faire pousser de la nourriture sur la Lune ou Mars. Les scientifiques étudieront aussi comment gérer l’espace pour les plantes afin qu’elles ne prennent pas trop de place.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Les essais de la NASA avec fraises, concombres et basilic citron rapprochent la nourriture fraîche et saine pour les astronautes des futures missions sur la Lune et Mars.
articles.personality_title_es: La NASA estudia fresas, pepinos y hierbas para comida fresca en misiones a la Luna y Marte
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La NASA se está preparando para viajes largos a la Luna y Marte. Para ayudar a los astronautas a mantenerse saludables y contentos lejos de la Tierra, los científicos buscan cultivos que puedan crecer en el espacio y ofrecer alimentos frescos.

**Qué pasó** – Investigadores han probado fresas, pepinos y albahaca limón en cámaras especiales que imitan las condiciones espaciales. Descubrieron que las fresas como la variedad 'Delizz' crecen bien y producen frutas sabrosas. Los pepinos, un nuevo cultivo espacial, también dieron frutos constantes. La albahaca limón, una hierba con aroma a limón, pasó las pruebas iniciales y se probará más en la Estación Espacial Internacional.

**Impacto** – Cultivar estas plantas en el espacio es importante porque no solo proporcionan alimentos frescos, sino que también ayudan a reciclar el aire y el agua dentro de las naves. Las hierbas y frutas frescas hacen las comidas más agradables, lo que ayuda a los astronautas a no aburrirse de su comida. Esta variedad también apoya su salud y bienestar mental durante las misiones largas.

**Próximo paso** – La NASA seguirá probando estas plantas en la Estación Espacial Internacional usando una nueva cámara de cultivo. Esto dará más información sobre cómo cultivar alimentos con éxito en la Luna o Marte. Los científicos también estudiarán cómo manejar el espacio para las plantas para que no ocupen demasiado lugar.

**Resumen en una frase** – Las pruebas de la NASA con fresas, pepinos y albahaca limón acercan la comida fresca y saludable para los astronautas en futuras misiones a la Luna y Marte.
